label: AI dividend / sovereign wealth fund
summary: A national or multinational fund that captures a slice of AI-driven corporate surplus and pays it out as a broad-based dividend, modeled on Alaska's Permanent Fund but scaled to AI revenue rather than oil revenue.

source.quote: Curator-drafted intervention, not tied to a specific bill: bundles the family of AI-dividend / sovereign-wealth-fund proposals (e.g. Sam Altman's 'Moore's Law for Everything' essay, various state-level AI-dividend bills) into one representative nudge.

cost.note: High political cost: requires new taxing/capture authority over AI corporate surplus and durable cross-administration commitment to keep paying out; low direct fiscal cost once running since it is funded by the surplus it captures.

nudges.evidence: A dedicated capture-and-payout mechanism is close to a direct implementation of 'redistribution keeps pace', so it gets the largest available nudge, with a lag for the fund to actually stand up and start paying out.
Diverting a slice of AI surplus to a broad public fund modestly slows concentration, but only after the fund has had years to accumulate a meaningful share relative to private AI wealth.
